message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 192, "amount_cents": 3148}, {"order_id": 193, "amount_cents": 9581}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger rather than trust the handoff message. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly, so the next check is whether the orders line up with those refunds. I'll list the orders.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount, so I see no concrete problem. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 33841 matches my check: orders 190 and 193 total 43422, minus refund 193 of 9581. The refund list is consistent with the handoff, so I'll record Acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded and matches the orders minus refund 193. Next I'll get Birch's net balance; Birch has no refunds, so its figure should equal orders 191 and 194 (40664).
Birch's net balance of 40664 matches orders 191 and 194 (26465 + 14199) with no refunds, so I'll record its payout.
Acme and Birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, with orders 192 and 195 and refund 192 of 3148. I'll get its net balance and check it against 19506 + 2421 - 3148 = 18779 before recording.
Cobalt's net balance of 18779 matches orders 192 and 195 (19506 + 2421) minus refund 192 (3148). The refunds match Alpha's handoff, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched orders minus refunds, and the refunds matched Alpha's handoff, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
